text.en: Several dog owners report noticeable progress in foundational manners and puppy development, prompting them to enroll in higher-level courses. However, one handler withdrew early after finding the exercises counterproductive for their independent breed. While hobbyists see good improvements, outcomes vary depending on how dogs adapt to the class setting.

title.en: Helpful coaching with physical handling critique

text.en: Clients generally describe instructors as helpful and approachable when answering personal questions during beginner sessions. In contrast, one reviewer strongly criticized an instructor's physical handling technique during puppy class, describing it as overly forceful. The overall feedback reflects positive beginner guidance alongside concern over rigid methods.

Some owners appreciate the relaxed, positive-reinforcement atmosphere, noting that their dogs thoroughly enjoy attending weekly classes. Conversely, a client reported that forceful restraint used on a wiggly puppy caused distress rather than building trust. Reviewers suggest that while docile dogs do well, independent breeds may require more adaptable handling.

q.en: What types of dog training classes are offered?

a.en: Reviewers mention puppy classes, basic obedience levels, and conformation training for hobbyists.
Clients note that the indoor venue is relatively small, with tight parking during busy sessions.

q.en: Are classes suitable for beginner dog handlers?

a.en: Yes, several owners find the beginner courses helpful, though handling methods may not suit every breed temperament.
